name: forecast.accuracy
summary: Native forecast records with request-bound accuracy metrics.
purpose: Inspect one account and creation-query day, retaining the approved legacy accuracy projection without recalculating metrics.

list.description: Read complete bounded base records and all required native accuracy metrics.

parameters.name: record-date
parameters.description: Native creation-query day YYYY-MM-DD; distinct from returned valueDate/baseValueDate.

identity_description: Native nonempty base record id; every id retains its independently request-bound metrics.

fields.name: accuracy
fields.meaning: Approved native metric fields, unscaled, bound by this record in the metric request.

limitations: One explicit account and one native creation-query day. Full creation-time range 000000 through 235959; source timezone remains unknown.

GET /bankCashForecastRecordAccuracyQuery.json once with fixed width5000; require arrivals=unique native id=result.count and at most100 base rows before metric calls. The100 limit is a client budget, not a backend capacity statement.

GET /cashFlowDetailDay.json once per base row, bound to native id/valueDate/accountNo/instId/currency/bankId/forecastBalance and selected alias. Metric roots do not echo record id; association is the exact request binding.

Preserve the pinned legacy 12 base fields plus11 scalar metric fields under accuracy; excluded base context, unknown fields and other UI sections are not added to the public projection. Missing projected fields remain null, native empty strings and raw ratios remain unchanged.
Native zero-balance strings0.0/0.00 use request value0 only, matching frontend binding; output forecastBalance is unchanged.

Every required query shares host transport, retry, request allowance and deadline. Business/auth/schema/binding failures abort without publishing partial output. No new Get, detail cache, Duckdog import or legacy runtime dependency.

Live does not publish. Complete nonempty refresh and offline replay preserve the same composed records; empty/failed refresh preserves the previous capture. Record-date denotes the original query and is not a local filter over valueDate.
